svg.title: Choosing a distribution
svg.desc: Start with the variable and its support. Follow discrete or continuous questions to candidate families, then check assumptions and fit. All seventeen implemented pre-release API surfaces are included. This is not automatic model selection.

g.text: VBA PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS
Choosing a distribution
Start with the variable. Check the mechanism. Compare candidate models.
1 DEFINE WHAT X MEASURES
Counts or measurements? What values are possible? Fixed trials, exposure or stopping rule?
These routes can overlap. A matching support narrows the options; it does not establish a good fit.
2A DISCRETE · counts / integer outcomes
Successes in a fixed number of trials?
→ Binomial
Independent Bernoulli trials; fixed n and p.
Changing p or dependence needs another model.
Sampling a finite population without replacement?
→ Hypergeometric
max(0, n − N + K) ≤ k ≤ min(n, K)
Uniform random sample: size n from N, K successes.
The population composition is fixed.
Events over a fixed exposure?
→ Poisson
Independent increments and a constant event rate.
Check exposure, clustering and mean versus variance.
Failures before success number r?
→ Geometric / Negative Binomial
Independent Bernoulli trials with constant p.
r = 1: Geometric; r ≥ 1: Negative Binomial.
Equally likely consecutive integers?
→ Discrete Uniform
Every integer in the finite range has equal mass.
Bounds must describe the actual sample space.
2B CONTINUOUS · measurements / statistics
Real-valued and approximately symmetric?
→ Normal / Student t / Standard Normal
x ∈ ℝ
Normal-shaped or heavier, t-shaped tails?
Standard Normal is the fixed N(0,1) surface.
Positive quantity with a Normal log?
→ Lognormal
Check log-scale fit and multiplicative variation.
Zeros and negative values do not fit this model.
Nonnegative duration or lifetime?
→ Exponential / Gamma / Weibull
Constant hazard: Exponential; flexible shape: Gamma.
Monotone hazard: Weibull; account for censoring.
Continuous proportion or bounded measurement?
→ Beta / Uniform
Beta: flexible shape on [0,1]; rescale if needed.
Uniform: constant density, not just bounded data.
A statistic with a known sampling construction?
→ Chi-square / F
Chi-square: sum of independent squared N(0,1)s.
F: ratio of independent chi-squares / their df.
3 CHECK THE CANDIDATES BEFORE USING THEM
Check support, zeros, rounding, truncation, censoring, dependence and stability over time.
Estimate parameters; examine probability plots, tail fit and out-of-sample performance.
Reject inadequate models. Similar means or a good histogram alone do not validate the choice.
4 CHECK THE IMPLEMENTATION AND ITS LIMITS
Confirm parameter conventions, supported operations, accuracy contracts and known limitations.
Geometric / Negative Binomial count failures, not trials. Beta has no point mass at 0 or 1.
CURRENT API / PRE-RELEASE · 17 surfaces, reconciled with the Distribution Map.
Planned noncentral distributions and dependence extensions are outside this guide.
Examples: defects in n items → Binomial; waiting with constant hazard → Exponential (if assumptions hold).
Companion: docs/visuals/choosing-distribution.md · No automatic selection or release certification.
